title: the model servers run with CUDA graphs: --enforce-eager off in every serving profile
note: basis 'shown' means shown by the tree, the card's tests and the bench's comment on #639 of 2026-11-22 10:08 UTC; nothing was run on a GPU.

findings.claim: the vendor's RTX PRO 6000 serving record was taken with --enforce-eager and still passes tools/serving_config.py measured, which does not compare a record's eager flag with the profile's; it now notes the difference on stderr only; a refusing check would block the RTX PRO 6000 install until the bench's record on the new setting lands

start time to healthy, card memory at start and at peak at the profiles' own fractions, throughput and the 5090's wake time are not measured with CUDA graphs on; the health-check start periods, install waits and the tier record's free_memory_at_peak_mib were set or measured with eager on

the bench's label comparison ran at a memory fraction of 0.9, not at the profiles' fractions (0.40 and 0.20 on the RTX PRO 6000); graphs' memory comes out of each server's fraction, so the KV cache at the shipped fractions is not measured
